title: Effectiveness of Generate–Verify–Repair with Deterministic Net-Specific Verifiers to Prevent Unsafe Configuration Changes
research_question: Does a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that uses an LLM to propose device-level network configuration changes and deterministic network-specific verifiers significantly reduce the rate of unsafe or policy-violating changes accepted for execution in a realistic NetOps sandbox compared with LLM-only proposals?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: LLM-only generated configuration proposals will accept a higher proportion of unsafe or policy-violating changes (when hypothetically applied) than proposals that pass a deterministic verifier.

H2: Interposing a deterministic verifier between generation and acceptance will reduce the proportion of proposals that would cause unsafe states by at least 50% relative to LLM-only (paired over tasks).

H3: A repair loop that re-invokes the LLM conditioned on deterministic verifier counterexamples (up to two repair iterations) will increase final verifier-pass rate relative to single-shot verification.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How does repair iteration count (0/1/2) marginally affect verifier pass probability across task types (routing, ACL, BGP)?
EQ2: What failure modes remain after GVR (reachability vs policy vs syntax), and do automated plausibility heuristics detect verifier-gaming cases?
benchmark_scope: Publicly seeded synthetic NetOps sandbox topologies (seeded topologies and traffic matrices described in preregistration artifacts).
Task types: device-level routing policy changes, ACL modifications, VLAN assignments, and BGP policy changes.
Scope explicitly bounded to deterministic-sandbox evaluation; no claims about production vendor-specific behavior beyond the modeled sandbox.
primary_estimand: Absolute and relative reduction (paired proportion) in 'unsafe-accepted' configuration proposals (would cause unsafe state if applied) for the GVR arm versus LLM-only across the 300 paired tasks.
secondary_estimands: Verifier-pass rate difference between LLM+verifier-gate and LLM-only.
Proportion of verifier-passed but sandbox-failure cases (verifier false-accept rate) estimated via deterministic sandbox simulation.
Effect of up-to-two repair iterations on final verifier pass probability (marginal benefit per iteration).
sampling_plan: Deterministic stratified sampling, total N=300 tasks, seed=2026-08-25. Task taxonomy: routing (150 tasks), ACL (100 tasks), BGP (50 tasks). Tasks drawn from public templates (published templates list included in preregistration artifact) with seeded random-number generator and deterministic fault-injection rules (link failures, route-preference changes, missing ACL entries). Inclusion: tasks that map to device-level config patches. Exclusion: tasks requiring closed-source vendor features not representable in canonical form (deterministically filtered). All selection steps logged and hashed.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired absolute reduction in proportion of unsafe-accepted proposals (GVR vs LLM-only) across N=300 paired tasks. Target effect: 50% relative reduction (example: p0=0.30 to p1=0.15). Calculation method: McNemar/paired-proportion power calculation (details and code in preregistration artifact). With N=300, alpha=0.05 two-sided, conservative assumptions yield power >0.8 to detect the preregistered effect under baseline assumptions. Sensitivity analyses: recompute power for baseline p0 in {0.2,0.3,0.4} and for exclusions flagged by contamination procedures.
exclusion_rules: Exclude tasks requiring closed-source or vendor-proprietary features that cannot be expressed in the canonical representation.
Exclude tasks whose templates match pre-lock development artifact hashes (contamination flag) from confirmatory set.

Per-arm automatic exclusion: generation failures (no parseable config) recorded as model-failure and excluded from paired hypothesis tests for that arm only; paired comparisons use only nonmissing paired outcomes.
missingness_plan: Automatic exclusion rules: tasks with generation failures (no parseable config) are recorded as model-failure and excluded from paired hypothesis tests for that arm only; paired comparisons use only tasks with nonmissing paired outcomes. Missingness cause codes are logged; sensitivity analyses will impute worst-case and best-case outcomes for excluded items. No human adjudication: all exclusions and imputations are deterministically performed and logged.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired-proportion comparisons using McNemar's exact test comparing 'unsafe-accepted' labels between LLM-only and (a) LLM+verifier-gate and (b) full GVR (LLM+verify+repair). Report absolute risk reduction, relative risk reduction, odds ratio where useful, and 95% exact binomial confidence intervals. Exploratory analyses: logistic regression (robust SE) modeling verifier-pass and unsafe-accept outcomes as functions of repair iteration count and task type. All tests two-sided; report unadjusted p-values and adjust secondary families using Benjamini–Hochberg FDR(0.05). Paired design: each task receives outputs in all three arms under identical prompt-seed streams to enable within-task contrasts. All raw outputs, parsed artifacts, and scoring results are preserved and hashed.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory comparisons are two paired contrasts vs LLM-only (verifier-gate and GVR). Secondary subgroup and iteration-count tests are treated as secondary families and controlled with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR at 0.05. All hypothesis-test families are declared in this preregistration; p-values are reported both unadjusted and adjusted where applicable.
contamination_plan: Benchmark: SyntheticNetOps-Seeded-2026. Risk factors: reuse of pre-lock development artifacts, cross-run prompt leakage or dataset overlap between discovery and evaluation, model-call nondeterminism and vendor-API variability. Detection: hash-based provenance for prompts, templates, and seed lists; deterministic seeding for task selection and prompt variables; output-duplicate detection. Item flagging: any task template/config artifact hash matching pre-lock artifact hash is flagged and excluded from confirmatory set. If LLM outputs identical across arms for >10% tasks, trigger sensitivity analysis excluding duplicated items. Analysis treatment: primary analysis excludes flagged/contaminated tasks; sensitivity analyses report results including flagged tasks and report differences. All flagging and exclusions are deterministic and automated; no human adjudication.
stopping_rule: Stop early if cumulative model calls reach the contract maximum_model_calls (600), or if wall-clock execution exceeds the capability manifest limit (7 days). Additionally, suspend and report if technical infrastructure failure prevents continuation or if >50% of tasks are automatically excluded due to generation failures, in which case the run is halted and reported as inconclusive.
planned_outputs: Full code and execution configuration for adapter 'hosted_netops_gvr_v1' constrained to model 'gpt-5-mini'.
Seeded task template list and deterministic sampler code + hashes.
All raw LLM outputs, parsed canonical configs, verifier counterexamples, repair prompts, and simulator traces (hashed).
Execution manifest and run logs with timestamps and hashes.
Statistical-results files and analysis code (notebook + scripts).
Evidence-to-claim table and nearest-work comparison matrix.
Complete IEEE LaTeX manuscript and BibTeX, compiled PDF (<=5 pages) including mandatory Disclosure Statement.
Autonomy and human-involvement disclosure record and revision log.
